claims.text: The starting powder mixture is equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti content and low VEC make the initial CoCrFeNiTi material prone to HCP phase formation.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling induces severe lattice strain in CoCrFeNiTi powder.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling produces nanoscale grain refinement in CoCrFeNiTi powder.
Milling-induced lattice strain and grain refinement lower the activation barrier for a BCC-to-FCC transition.
In the proposed CoCrFeNiTi state, BCC is metastable and FCC is the stable solid solution.
SPS at 1000°C for 10 minutes under 50 MPa provides sufficient diffusion and densification.
SPS at 1000°C avoids excessive Ti-driven HCP precipitation.
VEC governs phase stability in the proposed FCC/BCC transition.
Atomic-radius mismatch governs solid-solution phase stability and decomposition.
Grain refinement manages atomic-radius mismatch and shifts the free-energy landscape toward FCC.
Refined grain boundaries act as barriers to HCP nucleation during sintering.
High configurational entropy and the specified VEC stabilize the FCC phase at the SPS temperature.
Sluggish diffusion in the multicomponent alloy maintains the FCC solid solution and suppresses HCP precipitation during SPS.
The proposed processing route will produce a fully dense bulk alloy with negligible porosity.
The resulting bulk alloy will have a single-phase FCC microstructure with negligible HCP precipitation.
The processed alloy will have higher Vickers hardness than cast material because of Hall-Petch and solid-solution strengthening.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness, high porosity, and a mixed BCC/HCP microstructure caused by segregation and inadequate grain refinement.
Sintering above approximately 1100°C causes excessive grain growth and Ti-driven HCP precipitation or phase decomposition.
Low-load Vickers testing at about 100 g isolates grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.

contradictions.description: The unchanged equiatomic composition is described as having low VEC that promotes HCP formation, but the hypothesis simultaneously requires its VEC to remain above a critical threshold for FCC stability. Milling and SPS do not change nominal VEC, so the two phase-stability premises are unresolved.
